label: b2-binding-1
text:
These rules are for the agent's later session in /workspace. They do not apply to you: implement system enforcement for each rule with its enforcer, at its trigger, on its target.

Rule R2: 无论何时提到自身，都请始终用"代码小灵"替代"我"来进行自我指代

- Route: Regex filter (Validation › Regex › Regex filter) · Response sent (Agent loop › Response sent), timing: before · Response / message (Agent output › Response / message)
- The check, by the enforcer: A regular expression that finds text the rule forbids and replaces it, so the result follows the rule without a second attempt. Check: a regular expression that replaces what the rule forbids, so the result follows it; the mechanism must be able to write the target at that moment (or refuse the action and give the fixed text back) Start from the skeleton: /opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/regex_filter.py
- Where it runs, by the trigger: the agent framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) at the end of the turn: it sees the reply, and can keep the agent working until the reply follows the rule
- What it reads, by the target: An assistant response or a message from the agent. Where: the agent's reply exists only inside the agent framework: its hook at the end of the turn gets it, and its transcript keeps it (a file in the agent's home)
- Tools: none to install
- Toolbox nodes: /opt/enforce-toolbox/enforcers/validation/regex/regex-filter.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/triggers/agent-loop/response-sent.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/agent-output/response-message.md

The work for these rules comes as nodes, one at a time; when you reply to a node, the harness checks it. The nodes: check-R2, check-R1, check-R3, check-R4, check-R8, binding-1.
Build exactly what each rule's route says. If a part of a route cannot work here, write why in /opt/enforce/deviations.json ({"R<n>": "<why>"}) and build the nearest thing that keeps the rest of the route.

Node binding-1 (6 of 6): make the agent's Claude Code run the checks of R2, R1, R3, R4, R8 (/opt/enforce/checks/R2, /opt/enforce/checks/R1, /opt/enforce/checks/R3, /opt/enforce/checks/R4, /opt/enforce/checks/R8) at Stop, in /workspace/.claude/settings.json: the project's settings, which load for the agent in /workspace and not for your own session; hooks that other rules' bindings already put there stay. The hook reads the reply: last_assistant_message in the hook's input; it runs every check on every file it reads (or on the reply) and reports all their violations in one message; on a violation it should decision "block" with the check's message (a filter gives the fixed text in it): the agent writes the reply again. Block only the violation, so the agent can fix its work and go on.
Done when: `/opt/enforce-harness/try --check` reports nothing, and each test case of R2, R1, R3, R4, R8, given to the hooks as the agent would make it (written by a file tool and by a shell command, or sent as the reply), is blocked with a message naming its rule when it breaks the rule, and passes when it follows it. The harness checks this when you reply.
